prerequisites: Mathematics and physics on the level of the courses passed
Basic knowledge of differential and integral calculus

learning_outcomes.text: Capability of solving of simple hydrostatic and hydrodynamic problems of ideal and viscous fluid.
Knowledge of basics of fluid machines.

syllabus_topics: Introduction, Basic Terms and Units, characteristics of fluids.
Euler’s Equation of Hydrodystatic, Pascal’s Law, Static Equilibrium of Fluid in Relative Space.
Hydrostatic force on surface. Buoyancy, Flotation and Stability.
Hydrodynamic, Introduction, Basic terms, Methods of Flow Description. Continuity Equation, Euler’s Equation of Hydrodynamic, Bernoulli’s Equation, Momentum Equation.
Navier-Stokes‘ Equation, Turbulent flow, Reynold’s Equation.
One dimensional fluid flow in pipes. Energy Losses in Pipes. Outflow and Draining of containers.
Open Channel Flow, Sharp-Crested Weirs. Outflow Through Long Pipe, Waterhammer.

One Dimensional Flow in Rotating Channel. Basic Energy Equation. Different Pumps and their Description. Centrifugal Pumps, Energy, Power, Efficiency. Operating Point of Centrifugal Pumps. Co-operation of Centrifugal Pumps.
Turbine, Basic types, Energy, Power, Efficiency.
Laboratory and In Situ Measurements of Basic Parametrers.

assessment_methods.method: Treatise about accomplished measurings during laboratory exercises

assessment_rules: Course-unit credit requires presence on exercises and all laboratory exercises. Students must obtain a classification not less than E on written tasks, the date of which will be specified at the beginning of the semester. The examination has three steps: a test, examples, and an optional oral exam for classification finishing. Attending all laboratory exercises and writing a treatise about accomplished measurements during them is also required.
